AssertionReference.description: Compact reference to an assertion without engine-production metadata.

CrosswalkDisposition.description: Decision a reviewed crosswalk makes for one source assertion.

CrosswalkLayer.description:
The crosswalk family's layer payload. Required when `type: 'layer'`, forbidden otherwise.

A crosswalk layer is how an organization covers source assertions its base crosswalk has never seen. Concepts local to that organization arrive through its own scheme layer, and the sold crosswalk above it structurally could not have mapped them; without a layer they translate as `unmapped`, which is safe but leaves a reviewer holding the decision. The layer's own `mappings` and `selections` are the additions and overrides, written as an ordinary crosswalk document; what it takes away is listed here.

Binding and merge rules are the cross-family ones: see `LayerBinding`. A crosswalk layer may add, override, and remove; later wins on a colliding id. The layer's `sourceScheme` and `targetScheme` must name the same pair its base does, since a mapping between one pair of schemes says nothing about another.

base.description: The artifact or layer this one stacks on, as `id@version`.

removes.description: Mappings and selections inherited from below that this layer takes away.

requires.description: Layers that must be present AND composed before this one. A layer that builds on what another layer introduced, or restores what another layer removed, only means anything on top of that layer, so the ordering is a load-time constraint rather than a hint.

restores.description: Mappings and selections an earlier layer removed that this one brings back, with the decision they carried below. Naming an element in both `removes` and `restores` is a load error.

mapping.description: The id of the mapping to remove.

selection.description: The id of the selection to remove.

CrosswalkLayerRemoval.description:
One element a crosswalk layer takes away, named by kind and id. Exactly one key.

The same reference-not-a-path reasoning as the scheme family: a mapping or a selection is addressed by the id it was reviewed under, which survives a storage change and validates as a closed set.

CrosswalkMapping.description: Reviewed treatment of one source assertion in a directional crosswalk.

authority.description: Authority or reviewed source behind the mapping, when one exists.

disposition.description: Whether the value is carried, reviewed, omitted, or forbids translation.

guidance.description: Operator guidance for applying or reviewing this mapping.

id.description: Stable identifier for audit and review.

source.description: Source assertion matched by this mapping.

targets.description: Target assertions. `carry` mappings emit these automatically; `review` mappings expose them only as proposals. `omit` and `forbid` mappings have no targets.

CrosswalkSchemeDependency.description: Scheme dependency declared by a directional crosswalk.

version.description: Required scheme version or semver range.

CrosswalkSelection.description: Cross-field decision that activates exactly one reviewed mapping candidate.

candidates.description: Ordered candidates; order breaks ties and places a fallback last.

id.description: Stable selection identifier for audit and review.

CrosswalkSelectionCandidate.description: One possible reviewed mapping set in a cross-field crosswalk decision.

authority.description: Authority behind the candidate decision, when one exists.

disposition.description: Treatment applied when this candidate is selected. Omitted, the candidate carries (`carry`).

guidance.description: Operator guidance for the candidate decision.

id.description: Stable candidate identifier within its selection.

mappings.description: Per-assertion mappings activated when this candidate is selected.

reason.description: Human-readable basis for selecting and applying this candidate.

sources.description: Source assertions covered when this candidate is selected.

targets.description: Targets emitted once when this candidate is selected.

when.description: Predicate used by a `first-match` selection; omission makes this the fallback.

CrosswalkSelectionCondition.description: Boolean test over source assertions used to choose a crosswalk candidate.

all.description: Every referenced assertion must be present.

any.description: At least one referenced assertion must be present.

none.description: None of the referenced assertions may be present.

CrosswalkSelectionStrategy.description: Strategy for choosing one candidate from a reviewed cross-field decision.

CrosswalkTarget.description: One target assertion a crosswalk can emit or propose.

copyValue.description: Copy the source assertion's captured value onto this target.

description:
Directional, versioned mapping between two schemes.

A reverse operation requires a separate definition. Directionality is explicit because a safe source-to-target mapping is not necessarily safe in the other direction.

citation.description: Primary citation for the crosswalk artifact.

description.description: Longer description of what this crosswalk translates.

guidance.description: General usage and review guidance for this crosswalk.

layer.description: The crosswalk family's layer payload. Required when `type: 'layer'`, forbidden otherwise.

mappings.description: How each source concept translates into the target scheme.

selections.description: Optional cross-field decisions whose selected mappings supplement `mappings`.

sourceScheme.description: The scheme this crosswalk translates from.

targetScheme.description: The scheme this crosswalk translates to.

type.description: What kind of document this is. Absent means `'crosswalk'`. `type: 'layer'` requires the `layer` block and `type: 'crosswalk'` forbids it, both enforced at load. Every layerable family wears this same envelope; see `LayerBinding`.
